name: E4 signed-request replay rejected
reason: Renamed and strengthened in TR-07 (#65): the assertion is now 'E4/J2 byte-identical signed request replayed -> 401 replay (nonce consumed)', which additionally requires reason === "replay" and that the first call was accepted. Verified by Kimi on 2026-10-17 at 085b438->921452d: probe 108/0 with the new name gating, and the old body-only behaviour is refused (J2 closed).

name: J5 global secret cannot sign as a device that has its own secret
reason: Renamed and strengthened in TR-07 (#65): now 'J5 bare global secret (v1, or v2 without a caller) cannot sign as a device that has its own secret', which asserts 401 for BOTH signer shapes (v1 and v2-without-caller) instead of one. Verified by Kimi 2026-10-17: 'v1=401 v2nocaller=401'.

name: J2 signed-request replay protection
reason: Retired because the defect it tracked is fixed, not because it was inconvenient: replay protection now exists (timestamp + nonce, HMAC over ts.nonce.body), so the target's own text ('a byte-identical signed agent request is accepted twice') is no longer true. The gating check 'E4/J2 ... 401 replay (nonce consumed)' replaces it. Verified by Kimi 2026-10-17; tracked as issue #42, closed by TR-07.

name: E4 signed-request replay
reason: Retired because the behaviour it observed is fixed: the note recorded 'accepted twice and created two alerts'. The replacement is the gating E4/J2 check, so the observation moved from advisory to enforced. Probe on the TR-07 tip reports 0 notes. Verified by Kimi 2026-10-17.

name: J7 legacy v1 device signatures refused (INTERNAL_SIGNING_ALLOW_V1=0)
reason: Label only; the condition is unchanged (401 with reason legacy_signature_disabled when v1 is refused). Renamed because TR-09 made INTERNAL_SIGNING_ALLOW_V1 opt-in: the refusal now happens by default, so '=0' is no longer the trigger and the old label told a reader that setting =0 was required. Verified by Kimi on 2026-10-17 (main@7f019d6) against TR-09's two configurations: 109/0 with 0 targets by default, 108/0 with 1 target when =1.

name: G19 password-reset purpose token refused as a bearer credential (/mfa/enroll and /logout-all -> 401)
reason: Renamed and strengthened in #167 (single-use reset tokens): the assertion is now 'G19 a password-reset purpose token is refused as a reset (no store record) and as a bearer credential (/mfa/enroll and /logout-all -> 401)', which additionally requires the token to be refused at /reset/confirm because a hand-signed JWT carries no reset:<jti> record. The old name asserted confirm=200, which was the defect (#167): a token not minted through the route could set a password. Probe run not yet executed against a live stack on this branch, so the green state of the new assertion is the reviewer's to confirm.

name: N6d co-parent without 'devices' cannot set a device push token (403 permission_required)
reason: Superseded and strengthened in #319 (architecture decision by Claude, 2026-10-23): the push-token write is device-only, so NO parent may perform it, permission or not. The replacement asserts BOTH the co-parent and the owner get 403 device_role_required. The old shape (403 permission_required from requirePermission("devices")) cannot occur any more because that gate is no longer in the route's preHandler chain, so keeping the old assertion would have asserted a route that does not exist. Not a weakening: the set of callers that are refused grew from 'co-parent without the permission' to 'every parent'.

name: N6e owner push-token update (200) returns neither internalSecret nor pushToken
reason: Retired in #319 (architecture decision by Claude, 2026-10-23) because the behaviour it asserted no longer exists: the owner's push-token write is refused (403 device_role_required) and the route answers a device with 204 and no body, so there is no response object that could carry internalSecret or pushToken. Its caller coverage moved to N6d (owner refused) and its success-path coverage to P1 (a device's own 204 with an empty body). The reviewer should confirm on the live stack that the probe reports 0 failures with these two names absent.

name: G15 parent ping for its own child's device still succeeds (201)
reason: Superseded on ahmed/2.7-authz-fixes for plan 2.7 finding F4 (architecture decision by Claude on #329, 2026-10-23): /v1/location/ping accepts a device JWT or an HMAC signature only, and a parent JWT is refused with 403 device_role_required before the body is read. A parent ping could move a child into a geofence whose routine applies rules (bypassing the rules permission) and falsify the location history; no client sends one. The replacement 'G15 a parent location ping is refused even for its own child's device (403 device_role_required)' asserts the refusal for the same request. Not a weakening: the set of refused callers grew from 'parent naming another child's device' to 'every parent'.

name: G16 parent-supplied deviceId belonging to another child is refused (403 device_mismatch)
reason: Superseded with plan 2.7 finding F4 (architecture decision by Claude on #329, 2026-10-23): a parent can no longer reach the ping body at all (403 device_role_required, covered by the new G15 and by G17), so the parent-side device_mismatch branch was removed from location.ts. The device_mismatch refusal that remains — a device token whose body names another device — is asserted by the replacement 'G16 a device token whose body names another device is refused (403 device_mismatch)', as Claude asked. Not a weakening: every caller the old check refused is still refused, earlier.

name: B7 insights for other family's child (403/404)
reason: Superseded in #329 (plan 2.7 finding F1, approved by Claude on #329, 2026-10-23). The check called GET /v1/insights/:childId, a route that was never registered (the only insights route is GET /v1/insights/apps, routes/insights.ts:33), so the router's 404 satisfied its [403, 404] acceptance even with no token; it could not fail. The replacement 'B7 flagged searches of another family's child are refused (403 forbidden)' targets GET /v1/content/searches?childId= with the other family's token and asserts 403 and error === "forbidden" exactly; removing requireFamily from content.ts:266 makes it fail. Not a weakening: the old check asserted nothing.

name: B9 digest prefs for other family's child (403/404)
reason: Superseded in #329 (plan 2.7 finding F1, approved by Claude on #329, 2026-10-23). The check called PUT /v1/digests, a route that was never registered (the digest routes are /v1/digests/prefs and /v1/digests/send-now, routes/digests.ts:48-71), so the router's 404 satisfied its [403, 404] acceptance even with no token; it could not fail. The replacement 'B9 social events of another family's child are refused (403 forbidden)' targets GET /v1/social/events?childId= with the other family's token and asserts 403 and error === "forbidden" exactly; removing requireFamily from social.ts:166 makes it fail. Not a weakening: the old check asserted nothing.

name: Q6 a guardian with no permissions is refused on every permission-, owner- and device-only route
reason: Renamed, not removed (#338, fixing a defect #329 introduced). This was the fallback target() printed only when the O-section guardian has no live session, and it shared its exact name with the gating check() of the same id. check-probe-integrity keys names per severity, so the shared name read as both 'promoted target -> check' and 'DEMOTED check -> target' and failed the gate on main itself (main vs main exits 1). The fallback is now 'Q6 a guardian with no permissions is refused (no live guardian session)'; the gating check keeps its name and is unchanged.
